goal: Add 180-day retention for the agent-run spine (agent_runs / agent_run_steps / agent_outcomes) to ArchivalPoller via straight batched DELETE, with a supporting-index migration (079).
non_goals: No rollup / cold-store table (unlike the api_costs arm) — no lifetime-aggregate consumer of the run spine exists.
No env-configurable per-table window — follow the hardcoded INTERVAL precedent of the existing six arms.
Do not touch account_audit_log / approval_audit_log — they stay deliberately keep-forever.
Do not change read.ts consumers, dashboard windows, or the governor/suspension logic.
No refactor/abstraction of the existing ArchivalPoller arms — add two new arms in the same shape.
user_visible_behavior: Terminal agent_runs whose ended_at is older than 180 days are deleted daily; agent_run_steps prune via ON DELETE CASCADE.
agent_outcomes whose occurred_at is older than 180 days are deleted daily (own arm; they do NOT cascade — ON DELETE SET NULL).
Opening a review whose runs are all >180 days old shows an empty handling timeline (getReviewTimeline runs:[]); the review row and response row persist.
The ArchivalPoller 'Archived' log line and saturation warnings include agent_runs and agent_outcomes counts.
invariants: Running runs are NEVER deleted (status='running' iff ended_at IS NULL, per agent_runs_terminal_consistency; the arm filters ended_at < NOW() - 180d, which excludes NULL).

agent_outcomes retention (180d) strictly exceeds the max dashboard team-summary window (90d, '90d' in WINDOW_PARAMS) AND the governor/suspension window (GOVERNOR_WINDOW_DAYS=7) — no consumer under-counts within its own window.
getReviewTimeline (per-review, no time filter) and judge-store.findLatestRunIdForReview (latest/live run) are unaffected by retention.
Batched DELETE (LIMIT 5000) + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, matching arms 4-6, so concurrent archival cycles keep accurate counts.
Tenant-scope and RLS audits stay green — the two new cross-tenant DELETE arms are allowlisted with byte-exact SQL snippets.
Migration 079 applies staging-first, both Supabase projects in lockstep; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (non-transactional, per the 065 header).
edge_cases: agent_outcomes.agent_run_id is ON DELETE SET NULL (not CASCADE) — without its own occurred_at arm, deleting old runs would orphan outcomes (run link nulled) and they would accumulate forever.
Delete ordering: outcomes arm before runs arm (matches purge-stages.ts) to avoid wasted SET NULL writes on outcome rows about to be deleted the same cycle.
Uniform 180d window across runs+outcomes: because occurred_at <= ended_at for any terminal run, an outcome whose run crosses 180d is itself >=180d old, so no permanently NULL-linked outcome survives.
Cascade fan-out: deleting up to 5000 runs cascades their steps in one statement — bounded by the runs LIMIT, same shape as arm 4's bounded work.
Batch saturation (count >= 5000) is reported via the existing saturated[] warning path so the next cycle continues cleanup.
existing_patterns_to_follow: worker/background/pollers/ArchivalPoller.ts arms 5 (notification_deliveries) and 6 (analytics_events): straight batched DELETE with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + count/saturation reporting.
supabase/migrations/065_archival_watchdog_indexes.sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on the archival scan column + non-transactional apply header.
scripts/ci/tenant-scope-allowlist.ts: byte-exact ArchivalPoller SQL-snippet allowlist entries.
tests_to_add: ArchivalPoller.test.ts: agent_runs arm deletes terminal rows with ended_at older than 180d and never touches running rows (ended_at NULL).
ArchivalPoller.test.ts: agent_outcomes arm deletes rows with occurred_at older than 180d.
ArchivalPoller.test.ts: the 'Archived' summary and saturation warning include the two new arms' counts.

Regression guard tying the retention constant to its consumers: assert 180 (retention days) > max(WINDOW_PARAMS.windowDays) AND > GOVERNOR_WINDOW_DAYS, so raising a consumer window past retention fails the build.
